daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

PDIP Chairwoman Megawati Soekarnoputri has declined to join the government, with PDIP emphasizing the refusal was not due to insufficient offers. The decision underscores PDIP's choice to remain in opposition despite being one of Indonesia's largest parties. Meanwhile, coalition party leaders are scheduled to meet President Prabowo today to discuss vice presidential candidates, a critical decision following the vacancy left in the second-highest office.

  • Sandiaga Uno has endorsed Dasco as fit for vice president, praising him as capable of solving government problems.
  • National Police Chief General Ahrie Sonta has been removed from his position as head of the Police Legal Division after being named a suspect in the wiretapping case targeting President Prabowo.
  • DPR member Sahroni stated that the exclusion of illicit enrichment from the Asset Seizure Law was a deliberate consideration during the legislative process.
  • DPD Chairman has proposed having three vice presidents, though a DPR member rejected the proposal as unconstitutional.
  • Fadli Zon has claimed to be a wiretapping victim from 2021 through 2026.
  • KPAI has requested the minimum voting age for first-time voters be raised to 18 years.
  • National Police Chief Kapolri Suyudi has swiftly uncovered two major cases in less than two months in office, including seizing 600 tons of narcotics which he suggested may be a world record.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia and the European Union have sealed the IEU-CEPA agreement to boost trade cooperation, with the deal granting zero tariffs on 90.4 percent of Indonesian exports. Trade Minister stated the pact will open new export markets and expand market access for MSMEs, representing a major milestone in Indonesia-EU economic relations.

  • DPR Speaker Puan Maharani attended the AIPA session in Manila, emphasizing parliament's role in ASEAN's future.
  • Indonesia and China are seeking to strengthen trade and investment ties, while Indonesia and Saudi Arabia joined hands to develop creative economy cooperation.
  • Indonesia and the Netherlands have strengthened waste management cooperation.
  • National Police Chief has sent a team to the Philippines to arrest online gambling fraudsters targeting Indonesian citizens.
  • A minister stated that national resilience was the key message at recent ASEAN and APEC summits.

Other

Three bodies have been found at the candy factory fire site in Serang, with 36 people still missing following the blaze. BNPB has confirmed the Baduy settlement fire was caused by cooking stove flames, while the Banten governor called for faster response to such disasters.

  • BMKG has warned of heavy rain across eight provinces amid a cyclone seed, while BNPB reported floods and strong winds hitting North Sumatra to Central Sulawesi.
  • Mount Ibu and Semeru have erupted hours apart, while a magnitude 4.2 earthquake shook West Sumatra.
  • The government seeks to empower 23 million social aid recipients through new programs.
  • Indonesia is advancing its forest carbon program in nine provinces and targeting global carbon trade from Japan's market to CORSIA.
  • West Java Governor Dedi Mulyadi has set the 2027 provincial minimum wage at Rp 3 million, a 29.44 percent increase.
